title: Paracentesis (draining fluid from the belly)
what: Through a small puncture in your belly, the doctor drains fluid that has built up. It is done with local numbing.
why: When fluid has built up in the belly, called ascites, and makes it hard to breathe, eat, or move, or when the fluid needs to be tested.
duration: usually 20 to 60 minutes, sometimes longer if there is a lot of fluid; fluid test results in a few days
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will decide if anything needs to change
If you had this procedure before

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Usually your blood clotting is checked first. The puncture spot is marked using ultrasound.

prepare.title: Bladder
prepare.text: Use the toilet before the procedure.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You can usually eat as usual. Check with the clinic.

steps: You lie on your back, sometimes turned a little to one side
The doctor chooses a spot on your belly using ultrasound
The skin is cleaned and numbed with an injection
A thin needle or small tube is placed through a small puncture
The fluid slowly drains into a container
The needle is removed, and a bandage is put on
feel: A prick and stinging from the numbing
Then pressure, but usually no pain
As the fluid comes out, breathing gets easier
after: You usually lie down for a while and have your blood pressure checked
The bandage may leak a little. This happens, and it is changed
Fluid may build up again. Your doctor will tell you what comes next
red_flags: Dizziness, fainting, or sudden weakness: call emergency services
Severe belly pain or a fever over 38°C (100.4°F): see a doctor right away
The bandage soaks through with blood, or fluid leaks for more than 24 hours

faq.a: The spot is numbed, so you usually feel pressure, not pain.

faq.q: Why does the fluid come back?
faq.a: The procedure removes the fluid, but not its cause. Your doctor treats the cause.

reminders.text: Belly fluid drainage today. Use the toilet before the procedure and bring a list of your medicines.
